title: 1989 AHSME Problem 22
statement: A child has a set of \(96\) distinct blocks. Each block is one of \(2\) materials (plastic, wood), \(3\) sizes (small, medium, large), \(4\) colors (blue, green, red, yellow), and \(4\) shapes (circle, hexagon, square, triangle). How many blocks in the set are different from the “plastic medium red circle” in exactly two ways? (The “wood medium red square” is such a block.)

solutions.text:
The numbers of alternatives for material, size, color, and shape are \(1,2,3,3.\) Changing exactly two attributes gives \[ \begin{aligned} &1\cdot2+1\cdot3+1\cdot3\\ &\qquad+2\cdot3+2\cdot3+3\cdot3=29. \end{aligned} \]

Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: For each attribute, count the alternatives different from the specified block
Choose a pair of attributes to change, then multiply their alternative counts
